finding.expected: Replace substring-based semantic-key rejection with a closed exact normalized reserved metadata/envelope-key policy (and retain the explicit machine-local path/private-value protections that are actually required). Exact prohibited metadata keys such as provider/model/session identity and nested audit-envelope keys must still fail closed, but ordinary semantic keys that merely contain those tokens must remain representable. Add regression coverage proving exact forbidden metadata is rejected while representative semantic keys such as provider_contract, model_policy, prompt_schema and chat_memory_dependency are accepted and remain fingerprint-bound. Do not weaken byte, depth, strict-JSON, nested-envelope, credential, raw-log or machine-local protections.
finding.issue: Candidate/audit privacy filtering is implemented as substring matching over arbitrary semantic mapping keys. Because _PRIVATE_PARTS includes tokens such as provider, model, session, prompt, chat and conversation, legitimate Brain-owned semantic fields such as provider_contract, model_policy, prompt_schema or chat_memory_dependency are rejected as if they were out-of-band private metadata. TASK-179 requires rejection of prohibited protocol metadata/identity and nested audit/private material, not semantic vocabulary that merely contains those words. The current heuristic therefore narrows valid ARCHITECTURE/TASK_AUTHORING semantic content and makes the supposedly provider-neutral protocol unable to represent some valid provider/portability architecture decisions.

original_constraints: The only production mutation surface is scope.modify. If satisfying the contract requires changes to Decision Packet, Brain Context/Flow Cards, Unified State, Runtime, Reviewer/Publisher, authoring ingress, provider surfaces, roadmap state, or any other file, fail closed back to Brain rather than widening scope.

Candidates and Stage-2 semantic material use strict UTF-8 JSON mappings, recursive CRLF/CR to LF normalization, finite JSON values only, closed protocol-envelope schemas, explicit byte/count/depth limits, and fail closed on duplicate/unknown protocol fields. Recursively reject protocol metadata keys for chat history, chain-of-thought, raw logs/evidence paths, credentials/secrets, local root/workspace/remote/host data, timestamps, UUID/random ids and provider/model/session identity from candidate and audit semantic material.

BP-4A structural validation must not import semantic authority from candidate content. It must not parse/revalidate a candidate as TASK/REMEDIATION/REPAIR, choose a correction, produce a verdict, call canonical verification, or hand CANDIDATE directly to lifecycle mutation. Existing downstream canonical validators/ingress remain required after BP-4A.
